[CHARACTERS: Lirael:F, Julian:M, the youth:F]

[TITLE: "The Price of a Changed Wish"]

[SYNOPSIS: In the Veilwood clearing, Lirael supervises her first First Sacrifice as the youth offers a rehearsed vow. When the girl redirects the wish toward Lirael’s buried loss, the misalignment ripples through the assembly and Fate answers before any hand can intervene.]

The youth’s voice rose clear across the crimson spiralgrass.

“I offer the discipline to finish my studies and train as a Sacrificiant.”

Her aqua skin caught the dawn light, Weave-Script flowing in soft loops of resolve. The assembled First Favored stood barefoot in their gossamer tunics, every face turned toward the kneeling girl beneath the mated-pair veil-canopy. I felt the weight of their alignment-sense pressing against mine, waiting for me to confirm the match.

She looked up at me.

The prepared words left her mouth and the next ones did not belong to the rite.

“I wish instead that Lirael finds the father who abandoned her.”

The shift landed like a wrong note. The sacrifice she had rehearsed belonged to one desire; the words now asked for another. I felt the misalignment before anyone else could name it, the way the prepared price no longer pointed at the new request. My mouth was sealed beneath the gossamer band. I could only watch the Dohkar’s eyes narrow and the crowd’s posture change.

Julian’s memory cut through the moment: the way he had stepped between a family and a drunken merchant at the festival last turning, his long black hair swinging forward as he lifted the child out of reach without ever raising his voice. The image steadied me and then undid me; he would have known what to do with a broken rite. I wanted someone to see the girl’s mistake for what it was and not what it looked like from outside.

The youth’s coral hair trembled against her cheek. She meant the wish as a gift. She did not understand that the price she had already named could not cover the new desire.

Is this the moment the test begins — or the moment it ends?

The Dohkar’s hands lifted in warning. An elder at the edge of the gathering spoke low enough that only those nearest heard.

“Never hand Fate a blank page.”

The words hung. The girl’s Weave-Script stuttered from loops into jagged flickers. Fate does not announce itself with light. It rearranges what is already here. A woman near the front—someone the youth had trained beside—turned toward me with sudden recognition in her eyes.

“Your father crossed the Ascendant Run three turnings ago,” she said, voice carrying farther than she intended. “He asked after you at the ferry landing. I told him you were training.”

The crowd drew the only conclusion it could see: the wish had reached its target through me. The girl’s changed desire had pulled the answer into the open at the exact moment I tore the band from my mouth and stepped forward. Protocol broken. A supervisor reaching for her own ward’s rite. The qualification I had worked toward now sat on the edge of inquiry.

The youth’s face crumpled. She had meant well. The Dohkar’s gaze stayed on me, waiting for the explanation that would only make it worse.

I stood with the torn gossamer in my hand and the room watching. The girl’s sacrifice had been spent on a desire that did not belong to her. My intervention had looked like complicity. Julian’s remembered stillness felt suddenly far away.

My hand tightened around my great-grandmother's old tarot deck. I didn't remember bringing it. I toyed with the idea of letting the cards decide.

<<EXPANSION_A>>
I named the misalignment aloud before the Dohkar could speak. The room heard the truth from my mouth instead of their assumptions.
<<EXPANSION_B>>
I let the silence stretch. The woman who had spoken looked at the youth and understood without another word being said.
<<END_EXPANSION>>
